next_step: Start Dedicated POC (2-week) — provision canary pool + define eval prompts
notes:
Background:
- Mid-market product analytics SaaS; embedded insights in customer portals (B2B).
- High concurrency during business hours; bursty traffic from scheduled exports.
- Currently prototyping hosted API for feature parity; wants Dedicated for predictable throughput and data isolation if latency/cost align.

Recent activity / timeline:
- 2026-01-20: Initial inbound via docs download; AE outreach (Jordan).
- 2026-02-01: Discovery call — technical and procurement teams present (Maya joined). Notes: heavy focus on SSO + audit logs.
- 2026-02-18: Product demo of Hosted API; basic chat and embeddings tested. Fireflies ff_20260218_3429 attached.
- 2026-02-25: Follow-up pricing call; requested committed capacity numbers and sample TCO modeling. Gmail thread-fwd-CAJ9xY2U_B4 attached.
- 2026-03-04: Architecture deep-dive (network, KMS). SE (Maya) walked through VPC options. Fireflies ff_20260304_1182 attached.
- 2026-03-09: Internal execs signaled preference to move to a Dedicated POC before procurement approval.

POC goals and success criteria:
- Tech goals: demonstrate <100ms p95 token generation for chat baseline (100 concurrent users), sustained 500 reqs/min embeddings throughput with 200ms p95 when batching enabled.
- Reliability: show canary + fallback routing works: canary pool handles 5% traffic, automatic fallback to hosted-compatible model variant on capacity loss, region failover within 60s for simulated AZ outage.
- Cost/ops: validate cost-per-1M tokens with suggested batching and quantization profile; estimate savings vs hosted baseline.
- Security/compliance: confirm KMS integration for key wrapping, SSO provisioning, and audit log delivery to their SIEM.

POC scope & plan (agreed):
- Duration: 2 weeks (engineering POC) + 1 week for validation and exec review.
- Deliverables:
  - Provision Dedicated canary pool (small GPU set) in us-west-2 and us-east-1 for region failover testing.
  - Implement routing policy: 5% traffic to canary, 95% to existing hosted endpoint; automatic fallback to hosted API if canary saturated or health checks fail.
  - Model variants: baseline gpt-like open model (quantized) + higher-accuracy float variant for canary comparison; define automatic rollback policy to float variant vs hosted fallback.
  - Tracing and observability: per-route latency/cost dashboards (sample Redwood Console dashboard link in drive doc).
  - Run defined prompt suite (50 prompts) for quality regression checks and perf benchmarking.

Technical contacts and responsibilities:
- Horizon Crest:
  - CTO (Suresh Patel) — procurement & exec sign-off.
  - Lead Infra Eng (Ana Gomez) — VPC peering, network tests, provisioning windows.
  - ML Eng (Tom Nguyen) — prompt suite and quality sign-off.
- Redwood:
  - AE: Jordan Park — contract & pricing owner.
  - SE: Maya Liu — POC technical lead, handles provisioning and test plan.
  - Solutions Eng: Diego Ramos — observability and rollout configs.

Pricing sensitivity / negotiation notes:
- Horizon Crest wants committed capacity pricing for Dedicated but needs a 6–12 month runway to justify.
- Key ask: convertible credits — trial Dedicated credits applied to first 6 months of committed contract.
- They are cost-sensitive on embeddings throughput; asked for aggressive batching and cache guidance from Redwood Optimize.

Risk / blockers detail:
- Legal requires SOC2 + data residency clause in contract; legal_review ticket SEC-2121 opened.
- VPC peering windows: infra team has narrow maintenance windows (weekend only) — may delay provisioning.
- Exec budget approval contingent on POC demonstrating >=30% cost improvement vs current hosted run rate OR clear latency benefit.

Quotes / call snippets:
- "If we can get dedicated latency at predictable cost, this becomes an easy buy — execs just need numbers." — Suresh (CTO)
- "We need an actionable rollback plan if the canary introduces regressions — show us the tracing and the switches." — Ana (Lead Infra)

Next steps (short-term):
- Redwood SE (Maya) to send Dedicated POC runbook + provisioning ETA by 2026-03-12 (missed; follow-up scheduled).
- Horizon Crest to confirm maintenance window for VPC peering (Ana) — target 2026-03-18.
- AE (Jordan) to confirm trial credits sheet and draft SOW for 2-week POC.

Tracked metrics for POC (for handoff):
- p95 latency (chat) — target <100ms
- embeddings throughput (reqs/min) with batching — target 500
- canary error rate and automatic fallback success rate — target 0 failures in rollback tests
- cost per 1M tokens (with suggested batching/quantization)

Notes on fallback routing design (technical summary):
- Canary routing: percentage routing rule (5%) at the edge; health checks every 15s.
- On canary health degradation >2 consecutive failures, immediate 100% reroute to hosted-compatible model variant and alert to SE.
- Region failover: cross-region DNS + region-aware load balancer; simulate region outage by blackholing us-west-2 for 60s, expect failover <60s and no more than 1 minute of elevated error rates.
- Rollback plan: automated model variant swap + cache flush; retain last-known-good KV cache snapshot for faster warm start on rollback.

Internal AE notes (choppy):
- Exec cares about procurement simplicity; don't overcomplicate SOW.
- Try to push convertible credits offer; likely moves deal.
- Keep demo focused on canary rollback — infra will nit on that.
